acceptanceCriteria: Back-to-back merges to main each end with a completed (not cancelled) required-check run.
Pull request runs still cancel superseded runs.
The change names how the bridge precondition reads check state.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. Suspected and partly verified read-only: .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 8-10 declare concurrency group '${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}' with cancel-in-progress: true. For push events to main the group is the constant ref refs/heads/main, so a later merge cancels the in-progress run for the earlier main commit. When merges land close together a merged main commit can end without completed required checks, blocking the primary-main bridge precondition 'T required checks green'. The actual cancelled runs were not enumerated here. Expected: every main commit gets completed required checks (e.g. group by github.sha for pushes, or cancel-in-progress only for pull_request). Actual: earlier main runs cancelled. Related: CORE-GITHUB-MERGE-QUEUE-COMPATIBILITY-1.
title: CI for main pushes is cancelled by the workflow concurrency group, so merged main commits can lack completed required checks
